text:
Predicates:
PerformsInSchoolTalentShow(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows often.
AttendsSchoolEvents(x) ::: x attends school events.
Engaged(x) ::: x is very engaged with school events.
PerformsInTalentShowOrInactive(x) ::: x performs in talent shows often or is inactive and disinterested.
ChaperonesHighSchoolDance(x) ::: x chaperones high school dances.
AttendsSchool(x) ::: x attends the school.
WishesToFurtherAcademicCareer(x) ::: x wishes to further their academic careers.
YoungChildOrTeenager(x) ::: x is a young child or teenager.
Student(x) ::: x is a student who attends the school.
AttendsSchoolAndEngaged(x) ::: x both attends and is very engaged with school events.
NeitherAttendsNorStudent(x) ::: x neither attends nor is a student.

Premises:
∀x (PerformsInSchoolTalentShow(x) → AttendsSchoolEvents(x) ∧ Engaged(x)) ::: If people perform in school talent shows often, then they attend and are very engaged.
∀x (PerformsInSchoolTalentShow(x) ∨ InactiveAndDisinterested(x)) ::: People either perform in talent shows often or are inactive and disinterested.
∀x (ChaperonesHighSchoolDance(x) → ¬AttendsSchool(x)) ::: If people chaperone high school dances, then they are not students who attend the school.
∀x (InactiveAndDisinterested(x) → ChaperonesHighSchoolDance(x)) ::: All inactive and disinterested members chaperone high school dances.
∀x (YoungChildOrTeenager(x) ∧ WishesToFurtherAcademicCareer(x) → Student(x)) ::: Young children and teenagers wishing to further their academic careers are students.
BonnieEitherAttendsAndEngagedOrNeither(::: (AttendsSchoolAndEngaged(Bonnie) ∧ Student(Bonnie))) ∨ (¬(AttendsSchoolAndEngaged(Bonnie) ∨ Student(Bonnie))) ::: Bonnie is either both attends and is very engaged, and is a student, or neither.

Conclusion:
(AttendsSchoolAndEngaged(Bonnie) ∧ Student(Bonnie)) ∨ InactiveAndDisinterested(Bonnie) ::: Bonnie is either a student who attends and is engaged, or inactive and disinterested.
